existing_authority.resolution: Identity owns one-time generation/display-download, verifier-safe storage, individual consumption and operation/idempotency/version/audit lineage using the selected Identity/.NET stack.
Generate/Replace require fresh current exact-operation shared step-up; no browser-selected Account/policy/assurance authority or general session upgrade.
Consumption is evidence in the authorized recovery hierarchy. Do not invent an existing strong-factor session requirement, automatic final session, factor reset or full recovery completion.

Server generation and once-only handling/owner revalidation are already required. Existing /account/security plus transient card/dialog is a smaller route proposal; an independent page is not mandated.
Explicit processing/retention and security-notification owner contracts apply. No invented legal periods, universal adult-only gate, free-text mail or alternate Account lifecycle.

primary_sources.observed: Saved recovery codes include at least64 random bits; stored values are hashed and verification is throttled. Used codes are invalidated. The section also specifies subsequent saved-code issuance and replacement notification.
primary_sources.impact: Account for entropy after canonicalization when approving a supported saved-code profile. Do not silently implement auto-replenishment or notification effects: resolve009/011/016 owner contracts and active policy. No NIST/FIPS/deployment certification is claimed.

primary_sources.observed: SP800-63B-4 final was published July31,2025; it supersedes the prior revision.
primary_sources.impact: Use final Rev4 text, not earlier drafts.

primary_sources.observed: The default generator uses ten random positions from26 symbols plus a fixed separator. Its maximum entropy is10*log2(26)=47.0044bits. Generation stores a distinct sequence but returns the original list after the user update.
primary_sources.impact: Withdraw default-generator-as-preferred direction from frozen-v1; retain it as investigated history. Do not inherit its format/count or claim it satisfies the saved-code64-bit profile. The protected extension seam exists, but constructing a synthetic UserManager/store solely to access it is unnecessary if native .NET RNG directly meets the selected profile.

primary_sources.observed: The default store persists redeemable semicolon-delimited RecoveryCodes token strings and rewrites that token on redemption.
primary_sources.impact: No unchanged native recovery token store or fallback. Use recovery-owned individual verifier rows and owner transaction semantics; framework conventions are not Tunner lifecycle authority.

primary_sources.observed: The versioned salted native hasher operates on the supplied string; the generic user parameter does not supply owner or purpose binding.
primary_sources.impact: Reuse the native hasher with a recovery-specific supported work profile and an unambiguous purpose/Account/set/verifier-format input binding. Validate admitted format/cost/count before synchronous native hashing; a stopwatch alone cannot preempt expensive PBKDF2. No copied cryptography.

primary_sources.observed: Built-in cryptographic random-byte/string/hex generation APIs are available.
primary_sources.impact: Prefer an existing .NET RNG plus built-in encoding under one reviewed closed profile. Count distinct canonical code outputs, bound collision retries and measure entropy after formatting/canonicalization; no custom RNG or deployment-approval inference.
